reason: Under Security / How secure is my data, the quote states word for word that all new buckets have Block Public Access turned on by default; display is verbatim.
Read with its heading (Can I allow a specific Amazon VPC Endpoint access to my bucket?), the quote states bucket policies support the aws:sourceVpce condition to restrict access; the claim matches.
The quote lists exactly the ten algorithms in the claim, and the sentence before it places them on upload and download requests; display CRC64NVME is in the list.

The quote states the latest SDKs automatically calculate CRC-based checksums for all uploads and S3 independently verifies that checksum and only accepts objects after confirming integrity; the claim matches.
The quote states that when an SDK version without pre-calculated checksums is used, S3 calculates a CRC-based checksum of the whole object, even for multipart uploads; claim and display match.
The quote states that with an encryption client library you retain control of the keys, encrypt client-side, and only encrypted objects are transmitted over the internet to S3; display is verbatim.
The quote states S3 provides strong consistency for list operations so a listing after a write reflects the changes; claim and display match.
The claim restates the quote (new object or overwrite, subsequent read immediately receives the latest version) with no added scope.
The quote states strong read-after-write consistency automatically, without changes to performance or availability, and at no additional cost; both displays are verbatim.
The quote states no data transfer charge for a COPY within an S3 Region and pricing-page rates for a COPY between Regions; the claim matches both parts.
The quote states normal pricing applies to access by another account unless the bucket is Requester Pays, where the requester pays for requests and downloads; the claim matches.
The quote names lower-latency access in different geographic regions and a compliance requirement to store copies hundreds of miles apart; claim and display match.

The quote states Multi-Region Access Points manage requests across Regions, CRR moves data to create isolated replicas, and together they give a replicated dataset behind a single global endpoint; the surrounding answer confirms requests are routed.
The claim is the quote word for word, in the Billing answer on S3 data transfer charges.
The quote states no data transfer charge between EC2 (or any AWS service) and S3 within the same Region; claim and display match.
The quote supports only the independent line item on the monthly bill; the second half (Cost Management reports include it under Amazon S3) appears in the next sentence of the page but is not quoted.
The quote lists Object Tagging, Lifecycle, Object Lock and Replication, and a single bucket holding Deep Archive, Standard, Standard-IA, One Zone-IA and Flexible Retrieval data; the claim matches.
The quote states a minimum of 180 days of storage and a pro-rated charge for the remaining days on delete, overwrite or transition before 180 days; the claim matches.

The quote supports from $0.00099 per GB-month and about $1 per TB-month, but the claim's 'for data accessed once or twice a year' is only in the unquoted previous sentence, and the display '$1 per TB-month' drops the quote's 'about'.

Under the Deep Archive retrieval heading the quote states Standard is the default tier, within 12 hours, typically starting within 9 hours with S3 Batch Operations, and Bulk typically within 48 hours; all three values match.

Under the heading on recommended ways to migrate tape archives to Deep Archive, the three quotes name Tape Gateway with a VTL interface for existing backup applications, Snowball for terabytes to petabytes, and Direct Connect.
The quote states Deep Archive is up to 75% less expensive than Flexible Retrieval; claim and display keep 'up to'.
The quote states data is immediately deleted and cannot be recovered by AWS; claim and display match.
The quote names Object Versioning, Replication and Object Lock as optional features adding protection beyond durability, plus a backup application; the claim matches.
The quote states directory buckets only allow objects in S3 Express One Zone, which provides faster data processing within a single Availability Zone; claim and display match.

The quote supports up to 2 million TPS per directory bucket independent of directories, but the condition qualifier adds that default quotas are lower and increases go through AWS Support, which this quote does not state.

Read with its heading (Can I completely disable direct access using the bucket hostname?), the answer 'Not currently, but you can attach a bucket policy that rejects requests not made using an access point' supports the claim.
The quote supports S3 is designed for 99.999999999% (11 nines) durability, but the scope qualifier 'all storage classes' is not stated in the quote.
The quote states end-to-end integrity checking on every upload, verification of redundant storage before success, and periodic integrity checks of data at rest; the claim matches.
The quote states the durability system does not protect against accidental or malicious deletes and S3 relies on customers to decide what to keep and which controls to use; the claim matches.
The quote, following the SSE-S3 sentences, lists SSE-C, SSE-KMS, DSSE-KMS or a client library such as the S3 Encryption Client; the claim matches.
The quote states S3 applies SSE-S3 as the base level of encryption to all object uploads (since January 5, 2023); the present-tense claim matches.
The quote names EventBridge, SNS, SQS, or directly Lambda as destinations; both displays are verbatim.
The quote states Event Notifications can notify when S3 Lifecycle transitions or expires objects; claim and display match.
The quote states no additional charges for S3 event notifications and that you pay only for SNS, SQS or running a Lambda function; the claim matches.
The quote states event notifications can be set up based on object name prefixes and suffixes; the claim matches.
The quote states 40 KB of metadata per archived object, 32 KB at the Flexible Retrieval rate and 8 KB at the S3 Standard rate; all three values match.

The claim is supported, but the display 'Retrievals from S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval are free' drops 'Bulk' and reads as if all retrievals were free; the verbatim 8-word phrase 'Bulk Retrievals from S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval are free' keeps the condition.
The quote states a direct PUT with GLACIER in the x-amz-storage-class header and Lifecycle transitions from the active-data classes it lists; the claim matches.
The quote states that without provisioned capacity expedited retrievals might not be accepted during periods of high demand; claim and display match.
